description: A named power of two keeps a scaled capacity live as either input changes
code:
stage = 2
capacity = 5
factor = Math.exp2(stage)
scaled = capacity * factor
assert(scaled, 20)
stage = -1
assert(scaled, 2.5)
capacity = 8
assert(scaled, 4)
scaled

description: Base two scaling retains intrinsic input coercion while extra values are numerically ignored
code:
input = " 3 "
factor = Math.exp2(input, Date(99), [1, 2])
assert(factor, 8)
input = true
assert(factor, 2)
input = []
assert(factor, 1)
assert(Math.exp2(null), 1)
assert(Number.isNaN(Math.exp2()), true)
factor

description: Independent class powers recover when a missing exponent is restored
code:
class Gain(exponent):
    this.exponent = exponent
$Gain.factor = Math.exp2($Gain.exponent)
first = Gain(2)
second = Gain(-1)
assert([first.factor, second.factor], [4, 0.5])
delete first.exponent
assert(first.factor, null)
assert(second.factor, 0.5)
first.exponent = 3
assert([first.factor, second.factor], [8, 0.5])
[first.factor, second.factor]

description: A failed exponent update rolls back while an ignored optional read still controls deferral
code:
class Dial
dial = Dial()
dial.power = 2
scale = Math.exp2(dial.power, dial.optional)
assert(scale, null)
dial.optional = 9
assert(scale, 4)
try:
    dial.power = 3
    throw "RESTORE_POWER"
catch error:
    assert(error, "RESTORE_POWER")
assert(dial.power, 2)
assert(scale, 4)
delete dial.optional
assert(scale, null)
dial.optional = 0
assert(scale, 4)
dial.power = -2
assert(scale, 0.25)
scale
